Elden Ring Beginner Guide: Everything You Need to Know

2026-07-27•12 min read

Welcome to the Lands Between: Your Elden Ring Beginner Guide

If you have picked up Elden Ring and are staring at the screen wondering where on earth to start, take a deep breath. You are not alone. FromSoftware's open-world masterpiece is simultaneously the most accessible and most intimidating game the studio has ever made. This Elden Ring beginner guide is designed to give you the exact Elden Ring tips for beginners you need to not just survive, but genuinely enjoy the first dozen hours of the game without rage-quitting into the void.

We have boiled down hundreds of hours of collective playtime into the essentials. No fluff, no vague platitudes. Just the how to start Elden Ring advice that actually matters when you are standing in the Chapel of Expectation about to make choices that will shape your entire playthrough.

Pick a Starting Class That Matches Your Instincts

The single most common beginner mistake is spending ten minutes agonizing over the class selection screen. Here is the truth that veteran players already know: every starting class in Elden Ring can eventually use every weapon, spell, and piece of armor in the game. Your starting class determines your initial stats and gear, nothing more.

That said, some classes make the first few hours noticeably smoother. Here is a quick decision framework:

  • Vagabond — If you want a straightforward melee experience with heavy armor, solid damage, and a shield that blocks 100 percent of physical damage. This is the closest thing to an easy mode in Elden Ring.
  • Astrologer — If you prefer keeping enemies at a distance with sorcery. You get Glintstone Pebble right out of the gate, which melts early bosses.
  • Samurai — If you like fast, aggressive combat. The Uchigatana is arguably the best early-game weapon in the entire game thanks to its bleed buildup.
  • Confessor — A solid hybrid if you want melee plus a taste of healing magic without fully committing to a faith build.

If you genuinely cannot decide, pick the Vagabond. It is the most forgiving class for players who are still learning how combat works, and you can always respec your character later in the game.

Explore Before You Fight: The Golden Rule

The single most important piece of advice in this entire Elden Ring beginner guide is this: do not follow the main quest markers blindly. Elden Ring is not a linear game, and the path of least resistance almost always goes sideways, into a cave, down a cliff, or through a broken wall.

When you arrive in Limgrave after leaving the Chapel of Expectation, your instinct might be to charge straight toward Stormveil Castle. Resist that urge. The game is gently encouraging you to explore the open world first. Here is what you should do instead:

  • Head to the Church of Elleh first. Talk to Kale the merchant. Buy the cracked tear flask, the spirit calling bell (after resting at the Site of Grace and talking to Melina), and any crafting materials he sells.
  • Ride Torrent north and east. Clear out minor Sites of Grace. Pick up the Longtail Cat talisman from a cave. Loot every corpse you see.
  • Head south to the Stranded Graveyard. Grab the Scaled Set armor and the Spiked Club. Both are massive upgrades to your starting gear.
  • Clear out every cave and cellar you find. These mini-dungeons contain crafting materials, upgrade stones, and sometimes entire new weapon categories.

The idea is simple: the more of Limgrave you clear, the higher your level will be when you eventually reach the first major roadblock, and the more options you will have for tackling it.

Level Vigor First, Always

If you take only one piece of Elden Ring tips for beginners from this guide, let it be this: level Vigor above almost everything else for the first half of the game.

Vigor determines your HP. It is the single most impactful stat for survivability. A character with 30 Vigor will survive mistakes that kill a character with 15 Vigor. The soft cap for Vigor is 40, and the hard cap is 60. Until you reach at least 30 Vigor, prioritize it on almost every level-up.

After Vigor, invest in your primary damage stat:

  • Strength for heavy weapons like greatswords, hammers, and colossal weapons.
  • Dexterity for katanas, curved swords, thrusting swords, and bows.
  • Intelligence for sorcery builds using Glintstone staffs.
  • Faith for incantations, healing, and fire-based magic.
  • Arcane for bleed, status effect, and discovery-focused builds.

A common mistake is spreading your levels too thin across multiple stats. A character with 20 in four stats is significantly weaker than a character with 40 in one stat and 15 in the others. Specialize early, diversify later.

Upgrade Your Weapons Before Your Stats

Here is a secret that experienced players learn quickly: weapon upgrades often give more damage than stat increases, especially in the early to mid-game.

A +5 longsword will outdamage a +0 longsword even if the +0 version has 10 more points in the scaling stat. Smithing Stones are scattered throughout the world, and you should spend them liberally on your favorite weapon. You will never run short if you explore thoroughly.

The upgrade path works like this:

  • +1 to +3: Find Smithing Stone [1] in caves and mines.
  • +4 to +6: Find Smithing Stone [2] in slightly harder areas.
  • +7 to +9: Find Smithing Stone [3].
  • +10 (max for regular weapons): Find a Smithing Stone [4].
  • Somber weapons (unique boss weapons): Use Somber Smithing Stones, which go from [1] to [10] on a separate track.

Take any weapon you enjoy using to a blacksmith as soon as you have the stones. The damage increase is immediate and noticeable.

Learn to Dodge, Not Block

Many beginners come to Elden Ring from other RPGs where holding up a shield is the default defensive option. In Elden Ring, dodging through attacks is almost always better than blocking them.

Shields reduce your damage output because you need to lower them to attack. More importantly, many boss attacks will guard-break you, leaving you stunned and vulnerable. Rolling through an attack, on the other hand, gives you i-frames (invincibility frames) that make you completely immune to damage during the animation.

Here are the key dodging fundamentals:

  • Roll into attacks, not away from them. Most attacks hit in front of the enemy, so rolling toward them passes you through the danger zone.
  • Time your dodge to the moment of impact. Rolling too early wastes your i-frames. Wait until the weapon is about to hit.
  • Do not panic roll. Panicked mashing of the dodge button leaves you exhausted and vulnerable. Calm, deliberate dodging is dramatically more effective.
  • Learn each enemy's moveset. Every enemy has patterns. Once you recognize them, you can predict when to dodge instead of reacting.

Use Spirit Ashes Without Shame

Some players consider summoning spirit ashes to be cheating. They are wrong. Spirit ashes are a core mechanic designed by the developers specifically to make the game more accessible. Using them does not make you weak. Refusing to use them when you are stuck makes you stubborn.

The Lone Wolf Ashes you receive early from Melina are genuinely useful through a significant portion of the game. They draw enemy aggro, deal respectable damage, and give you breathing room to heal or reposition. Later ashes like the Mimic Tear become some of the most powerful tools in the game.

Final Thoughts

Elden Ring is a game that rewards patience and curiosity above reflexes. If you approach it with a willingness to explore, learn, and die occasionally, you will have one of the most rewarding gaming experiences of your life. Use this Elden Ring beginner guide as a foundation, but do not be afraid to forge your own path. The Lands Between have far more to offer than any single guide can capture.

Good luck, Tarnished. May you find grace.
